title: The Venus day-versus-year puzzle
author: NASA Space Place / NASA JPL-Caltech
date_basis: NASA Space Place article explicitly says last updated March15,2024; this is an update date, not initial publication.
content_access: NASA Space Place primary page re-read October7,2026. It directly distinguishes243-day rotation,225-day orbit,117-day sunrise interval, and reverse rotation. NASA Science corroborates rotation/orbit/direction but its sunset wording is not used here.
engagement_basis: Not applicable to this informational primary source; no popularity claim
truth_status: Scientific facts grounded in NASA; rounded values and day definitions must be preserved

grounded_beats.fact: Venus completes one rotation in about 243 Earth days.
One orbit around the Sun takes about 225 Earth days, so a Venus rotation lasts longer than its year.
A sunrise-to-sunrise day on Venus is different from a rotation: it lasts about 117 Earth days.
Venus rotates opposite to Earth and most other planets; the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.
The claim that Venus has a day longer than its year refers to its rotation period, not its sunrise-to-sunrise day.

forbidden_inventions: A Venus year is longer than one Venus rotation
All planets except Venus rotate in the same direction
Earth-like sunrise visibility through the clouds
A traveler or observer actually witnessed these events
Gameplay shows, measures, or simulates Venus
Exact unrounded periods beyond the supplied approximate values
An explanation for the cause of Venus's rotation direction
Calling the day/year statement famous, popular, viral or widely known: there is no sourced popularity evidence.

No generic intro, research-report cadence, false personal scene, or claim that background gameplay shows Venus. Draft exactly90–110words.

writer_brief.commentary: One short editorial observation about why definitions matter is allowed, marked separately; do not add scientific claims or a fictional observer
writer_brief.editorial_selection: Internally compare three hook approaches (contradiction, question, challenge); use the most concrete truthful hook and explain selection in rationale. This is a new video, not a revision of mail-merge.
writer_brief.editorial_refinement: Avoid school-report phrases such as "NASA says", "different measurement", "the famous puzzle works", or "that is why definitions matter". Source credit can remain offscreen. Open in immediately understandable language about a year ending before one complete spin. Explain the exact distinction clearly, then leave the backwards sunrise as the final punchline rather than appending a lesson about definitions. Natural conversational rhythm; concise causal explanation. Every scientific claim still needs a ledger beat.
